inputs.text: stained glass style depiction of a royal twin-throne finale, intricate details, vibrant colors, medieval grandeur: a single window panel of cut cathedral glass joined by thick black lead came with solder joints, glowing with its own jewel-tone light in deep reds, royal blues, greens and golds. On the left throne the king of spades with short silver-grey hair and black spade crown, his hair crown and black-and-silver armor all formed from shards of grey silver and black glass with ONLY black spade shapes as dark glass inlays across chest shoulders and knees, arms resting on the chair arms with defined gauntlet hands. On the right throne the queen of diamonds with very long red-orange hair past her shoulders and diamond tiara, both her arms fully visible resting on the chair arms with defined hands separated from her gown by lead lines, her hair tiara and white gown all formed from amber white and ruby glass with ONLY red diamond shapes as inlays, no skin no fabric no metal only glass. Behind them a tall arched window FILLED with a glowing narrative scene in opaque colored glass — a golden crown ringed by ruby roses and a radiant sunburst in blue and gold glass, luminous, no transparency, no view through it. Thrones of dark amber-brown glass, marble columns as cream glass, panel border woven with ruby blue and cream glass flowers. Glyphs: spade glass ONLY on him, diamond glass ONLY on her, no letters or text anywhere
